newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt no comment on Thomson decision.
newsitem.headline: French govt no comment on Thomson decision.

text.p: The French finance mnistry declined comment on Thursday on a newspaper report it could announce today its decision on the buyer of electronics firm Thomson SA.
"We are not making any comment," a ministry spokeswoman said.
Business newspaper Les Echos, citing industry sources, reported the decision could be made on Thursday. Lagardere and Alcatel Alsthom are rival bidders in the Thomson privatisation.
The government would initially only announce its "preference" in the sale, the ministry spokeswoman said.
The government, after announcing its preferred bidder, would pass the file to the Privatisation Commission which should give its opinion in the following weeks, the spokeswoman said.
The commission's choice should be the same as the government's, to allow the sale to go ahead and the decision to be made official, she said.

French newspapers consider Alcatel the likely winner as they view its offer as a "national solution" to the sale. But Alcatel is reported to be talking to Britain's GEC Plc as a potential ally for the Thomson-CSF defence unit and Samsung of South Korea as a partner for Thomson Multimedia.
Lagardere would sell the Thomson Multimedia consumer goods subsidiary to Daewoo Electronics of South Korea.
Thomson SA owns all of Thomson Multimedia and 58 percent of Thomson-CSF.
